Messages.Author: Hakuron
Messages.Body:
Name: Savoir Faire
Cardtype: Action
Cost: none
Capacity: none
Discipline: none
Clan: none

Lock any card that is not a minion as a -Action. If this acting minion is Black Hand the action is at +1 stealth.
If the action is successful, this acting minion may burn 1 blood to unlock (after resolving the action).
Anarchs get -1 intercept on this action.

Flavor text: Do you speak French?

Art notes: A well-dressed lady standing aside of an obviously sabotaged limousine talking to a mechanic.

World of Darkness reference: n/a

How does this card address a compelling game need?: Make possible interaction with permanents in play that are not minions.

Created by: Rudolf Garski

Messages.Author: jblacey
Messages.Body:
Wow, I forgot Remover was in the game. I have never seen anyone play that card. Okay, rules questions aside. The goal is: "Make possible interaction with permanents in play that are not minions." So the question is how do we temporarily disable a non-minion library card permanent on the table for a turn even if the card still functions while locked?

Here is my suggestion:

Savoir Faire

-Action flip a non-minion library card in play face down (face down cards do not affect on cards in play). The card flips face up during the controller's unlock phase. If this action is successful, the acting minion may burn a  to unlock. Black Hand gain +1 stealth and Anarchs gain -1 intercept during this action.
Flavor text: Do you speak French?

Messages.Author: Hakuron
Messages.Body:
Yes, »Savoir Faire« is inspired by »Remover« (and by »Fiendish Tongue«).
Thank you for your feedback, I now know what this card needs to be worth playing ...

Name: Savoir Faire v1.1
Cardtype: Action

Put this card on any card that is not a minion.
If this acting minion is Black Hand the action is at +1 stealth. Anarchs get -1 intercept on this action.
Lock that card; it does not unlock as normal during its controller's untap phase.
If the action is successful, this acting minion may burn 1 blood to unlock (after resolving the action).
Burn this card during your next unlock phase.

Of course, »Enkil Cog« is one of the worthiest targets for »Savoir Faire«, but (now) also »Dreams of the Sphinx«, »Helicopter«, »Tattoo Signal« become worthy targets (even if already locked).

> jblacey wrote:
> Are crypt cards in your uncontrolled region considered minions?

These are uncontrolled minions. But they can't be targeted unless stated otherwise:

> Rulebook wrote:
> Targets. If a card is played on another card, or selects or chooses or otherwise targets another card, the target card must be in play (i.e., controlled). Vampires in the torpor region are eligible targets by default, but vampires in the uncontrolled region and contested cards are not.

> Kraus wrote:
> Enkil Cog hasn't had a silver bullet yet, and one of the design principles was apparently supposed to be to include silver bullets to most cards, played or not.

But...

a) I have no idea where you're getting that principle from. Why would anyone create a design principle of creating silver bullets for cards that aren't played?

b) The proposed card isn't a silver bullet. Silver bullets have very narrow effects (such as silver bullets hurting werewolves, but not other supernatural things). The card as proposed is very broad in its effect. Yes, it might be suitable for hitting Enkil Cog, but it could affect a whole bunch of cards with 'tap to...' effects, and similar. This is pretty much not silver at all.

The whole point of silver bullets is that they specifically demolish werewolves but not, say, zombies or genies or fairies or dragons or beholders or cyborgs, and are probably pretty much crap against them. Messages.Author: Kraus
Messages.Body:
To be fair, I'm not sure if arguing about the exact definition of a silver bullet has that much relevance here.

If it leaves the card unlocked for a turn, it makes it much more playable against plenty of other targets, most of which are utility masters (Media locations, Stealth locations, Pool locations, Dreams of the Sphinx, Barrens/Ennoia's theater), some high-cap untap mechanics (Alastor+Helicopter) or Enkil Cog combo pieces (Enkil Cog, Metro Underground).

Frankly, I'm fine with that. We've only had contesting and 'burn location' effects to deal with those this far.

It won't be effective enough to win you games, most of the time, but there are plenty of 'wallpaperish' cards out there with niche effects that belong in the game and have a right to be there.

About the design principle, I'll admit I'm not exactly sure where I heard that from, so take it with a pinch of salt. Or a bucket load, whichever - I'm not here to back up anything because I can't recall the source, like, at all.  I should've probably added 'afaik' to even further emphasize how 'imo'-loaded that part was.

If it really escaped someone.

Simply put, I'm all for this card, as there's a very real real niche in the game for it, and it seems really balanced with lore-reinforcing thematics bound to it.

Krausedit\\ Whatever comes to the link James posted and it's arguments, that's a whole another topic.
